facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2005. The respondent filed for divorce in 2006 citing cruelty and desertion. A girl child was born out of this wedlock. The trial court granted a decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty in favour of the respondent-wife.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse cannot remarry during the pendency of an appeal.
legal_principles.held: The respondent cannot remarry during the pendency of the appeal.
cited_cases: Savitri Pandey Vs. Prem Chandra Pandey, 2002(1) RCR (Civil) 719

legal_principles.principle: A party to a dissolved marriage can marry again if the period for filing an appeal has expired or the appeal has been dismissed.
legal_principles.held: A party to the dissolved marriage could marry again if the period of filing an appeal has expired or the appeal has been dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: A court must make endeavour to bring about reconciliation between the parties before passing a decree.
legal_principles.held: The statutory duty has been imposed on the trial Court to make endeavour to bring about reconciliation between the parties.

legal_principles.principle: A court must endeavour to conclude the trial within six months from the date of service of notice on the respondent.
legal_principles.held: Every petition under this Act shall be tried as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made to conclude the trial within six months from the date of service of notice of the petition on the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A court must endeavour to conclude the hearing within three months from the date of service of notice on the respondent.
legal_principles.held: Every appeal under this Act shall be heard as expeditiously as possible, and endeavour shall be made to conclude the hearing within three months from the date of service of notice of appeal on the respondent.
